name: Seaweed / kelp foods (nori, wakame, kombu, dulse — dried, as sold)
native_basis_label: edible dried seaweed as placed on the market (DRY-WEIGHT basis, mg/kg dry matter) — never numerically compared to the wet-weight animal-seafood ppb
scope_note: Edible dried seaweed/kelp food products (nori, wakame, kombu, dulse) sold as dried, on a DRY-WEIGHT basis (mg/kg DM) — these numbers must never be numerically compared against the wet-weight animal-seafood ppb. Cadmium (500) and total mercury (100) bind the French CSHPF edible-seaweed maxima (confirmed tightenings from 2000 and 2500). Lead 5000 and total arsenic 5000 bind the Israel dried-seaweed lines; inorganic arsenic 1000 binds FSANZ. Nickel binds EU 2024/1987 seaweed 30000; tin binds the French CSHPF seaweed 5000. MeHg and Cr-VI are not-material (speciation-bounded); aluminium and total chromium are screened (no on-scope sovereign ML). Seaweed used as a dietary supplement (>=80% dried seaweed) routes to the supplements category, which carries the separate 3000 cadmium supplement line.

Pb.basis: dried seaweed, dry-weight (mg/kg DM). Israel FCS 2016 dried-seaweed Pb 5000; the French CSHPF edible-seaweed Pb 5 mg/kg DM (5000) concurs at the same value on the same dry-matter basis.

Cd.basis: dried seaweed, dry-weight (mg/kg DM). CONFIRMED TIGHTENING (2026-08-14): the French CSHPF edible-seaweed cadmium maximum of 0.5 mg/kg DM (500) — tabulated verbatim in ANSES opinion 2017-SA-0070 Table 3, enforced by DGCCRF — binds, replacing the prior Thailand dried-seaweed 2000 (retained as looser concurring context). Dry-matter basis matches the cell exactly.

tAs.basis: dried seaweed, dry-weight (mg/kg DM); total arsenic. Israel FCS 2016 dried-seaweed total-As 5000 (no stricter dried-seaweed total-As sovereign; France sets iAs not tAs for seaweed).

iAs.basis: dried seaweed, dry-weight (mg/kg DM); inorganic arsenic. FSANZ Schedule 19 seaweed iAs 1000 (HK Cap 132V seaweed iAs 1000 concurs); the French CSHPF seaweed iAs 3000 and Singapore 2000 are looser and not adopted.

tHg.basis: dried seaweed, dry-weight (mg/kg DM); total mercury. CONFIRMED TIGHTENING (2026-08-14): the French CSHPF edible-seaweed total-mercury maximum of 0.1 mg/kg DM (100) — ANSES 2017-SA-0070 Table 3, enforced by DGCCRF — binds, replacing the prior Israel dried-seaweed 2500 (retained as looser concurring context). The French 'Mercury' value is TOTAL mercury (matches this tHg cell). Dry-matter basis matches the cell exactly.

MeHg.rationale: Methylmercury is bounded by total mercury (MeHg <= tHg). No jurisdiction sets a seaweed methylmercury ML (all sovereign MeHg limits are fish/fishery scope), and seaweed is a marine primary producer into which methylmercury does not biomagnify (it biomagnifies up the food chain, not into algae), so MeHg is a negligible fraction of total mercury and is bounded by the tHg ceiling (tightened to France 100 DM). Audit-affirmed (2026-08-14).
MeHg.reference_method: Total-mercury screen; reflex MeHg speciation cannot exceed the tHg ceiling.
MeHg.regulatory_basis: Bounded by the total-Hg seaweed ceiling (France CSHPF, 100 DM); no seaweed MeHg ML anywhere

Ni.basis: seaweed nickel. EU Reg. 2024/1987 nickel in seaweed (except wakame) 30000 (Switzerland VHK 2026 'Seetang' 30000 concurs); the wakame variant (40000) is looser. This is the sole sovereign nickel limit reaching a seafood form.

Sn.basis: dried seaweed, dry-weight (mg/kg DM); tin. Unlike animal seafood (where tin is a can-migration-only analyte), the French CSHPF sets an edible-seaweed tin maximum of 5 mg/kg DM (5000) — ANSES 2017-SA-0070 Table 3 — because seaweed accumulates tin/organotin from seawater; it binds directly on the dry-matter basis, so this cell is a regulatory-alignment limit, not a not-material screen.

Al.rationale: No credible regulator sets an aluminium contaminant ML for seaweed. Seaweed accumulates aluminium from seawater/sediment as background; dietary aluminium is managed by weekly intake against the EFSA/JECFA TWI, not by a per-food maximum level. Screened rather than aligned to a non-existent ML.
Al.reference_method: Total-aluminium screen (ICP-MS); managed by intake vs the EFSA/JECFA TWI; no seaweed contaminant Al ML to align to.
Al.trigger: periodic aluminium screen; flag on anomalous elevation

Cr.rationale: No jurisdiction sets a total-chromium maximum level for seaweed or edible algae (the HK Cap 132V total-Cr limits are fish/crustacean/oyster animal-seafood scope, and the China GB 2762 total-Cr limits are cereals/beans plant scope — neither is on-scope for a marine macroalga). Chromium(III) is an essential nutrient; trace chromium in seaweed is geologic uptake. Screened as the substrate for reflex Cr-VI speciation rather than aligned to a mis-scoped number.
Cr.reference_method: Total-chromium screen (ICP-MS); substrate for reflex Cr-VI speciation; no on-scope sovereign seaweed total-Cr ML.
Cr.trigger: reflex Cr-VI speciation only if total chromium is anomalously elevated

Cr-VI.rationale: Cr-VI is bounded by the total-chromium screen (Cr-VI <= total Cr); no jurisdiction sets a Cr-VI food ML and there is no chromate pathway in seaweed (no lead-chromate adulteration as in spices), so any trace chromium is geologic chromium(III). Rebuttable if a routed source reports hexavalent chromium in seaweed.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Bounded by the total-chromium screen; reflex Cr-VI speciation only on anomalously elevated total chromium.
Cr-VI.regulatory_basis: No Cr-VI food ML anywhere; bounded by total chromium; no chromate-adulteration pathway in seaweed
Cr-VI.jurisdictions_checked: EU; Codex; US-FDA; HK; EPA (water only)

method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default; explicit-id lookup; MeHg speciation-bounded by tHg on animal seafood; seaweed on dry-matter basis)
